deep.reconstruction:
Context from the preceding page: one seeks three rational numbers with abc(a+b+c)=1, which feeds the question of five sixth powers summing to a sixth power. Write c=c, b=βc, a=α(β+1)c. Then abc(a+b+c)=α(α+1)β(β+1)^2 c^4. So one needs α(α+1)β(β+1)^2 to be a fourth power, equal to 1/c^4. J. A. Euler had taken β=4α(α+1) and α=2/(p^2-2).

Items 1-2: alternative parameter pairs that make F(α,β)=α(α+1)β(β+1)^2 a fourth power.
(1) α=8k^2/(2k^2-1)^2, β=2k^2. Then α+1=(2k^2+1)^2/(2k^2-1)^2 and β+1=2k^2+1, so F=16k^4(2k^2+1)^4/(2k^2-1)^4.
(2) α=1/(2k^2-1), β=8k^2/(2k^2-1)^2. This is exactly J. A. Euler's solution with p=2k. Here F=16k^4(2k^2+1)^4/(2k^2-1)^8.
The 'sive' alternatives β→1/β rest on the stated lemma. Since (1/b)(1/b+1)^2 = b(b+1)^2/b^4, replacing β by 1/β multiplies F by a fourth power.

Item 3 (lemma): if kx(mx^2+n) is a square at x=a, it is also a square at x=n/(ma). Indeed the value there equals ka(ma^2+n)·n^2/(m^2a^4).

Problem: find p,q,r with (p^2-q^2)(q^2-r^2) a fourth power. Euler's examples:
- (51,3,1) gives 2592·8 = 12^4.
- (14,13,11) gives 27·48 = 6^4.
- (29,25,23) gives 216·96 = 12^4.

Transformations (p,q,r)→(p+2q∓r, p±r, p-2q∓r). In each case p'-q', p'+q', q'-r', q'+r' are 2(q∓r), 2(p+q), 2(q±r), 2(p-q). Hence the new value is 16 times the old one.
- From (51,3,1) these give (56,52,44)=4(14,13,11) and (58,50,46)=2(29,25,23).

Reduction to the earlier problem: take q=a+b, r=a-b, p=a+b+2c with abc(a+b+c)=1. Then:
- q^2-r^2=4ab;
- p^2-q^2=4c(a+b+c)=4/(ab), so p=√(q^2+4/(ab));
- the product is 16abc(a+b+c)=16=2^4.

Example: a=3/2, b=4/3, c=1/6 gives q=17/6, r=1/6, p=19/6, i.e. (19,17,1) with 72·288=12^4. The transforms give:
- (52,20,±16), which scales to (13,5,4) with value 6^4;
- (54,18,±14), which scales to (27,9,7) with value 12^4.

General family: Euler takes J. A. Euler's b and c with p→k as his a,b, namely a=4k/(k^2+2), b=(k^2-2)^2/(2k(k^2+2)). Then:
- q=(k^2+2)/(2k);
- r=±(k^4-12k^2+4)/(2k(k^2+2));
- p=(k^2+2)^2/(2k(k^2-2)).
Cleared of denominators: p=(k^2+2)^3, q=(k^2-2)(k^2+2)^2, r=(k^2-2)(k^4-12k^2+4). For k=2 this gives (216,72,-56)=8(27,9,-7), value 96^4.
In terms of a,b,c the transforms become p'=a+2b+c, q'=a+c, r'=a-c and p'=2a+b+c, q'=b+c, r'=b-c. These are just the same construction with the roles of a,b,c permuted.

Alia analysis: put a=x/s, b=y/s, c=z/s. The condition becomes xyz(x+y+z)=s^4. Euler sets s^2=(x+y+z)p, so xyz=(x+y+z)p^2. This gives z=(x+y)p^2/(xy-p^2), x+y+z=xy(x+y)/(xy-p^2), and s^2=xyp(x+y)/(xy-p^2). This is continued on p.240.

Remark (mine): with sides y+z, z+x, x+y, Heron's formula gives area^2=xyz(x+y+z). So the condition is a rational triangle whose area is a square.
errors: 'p=a+b±2c': only the + sign works. With p=a+b-2c one gets p^2-q^2=4c(c-a-b), not 4c(a+b+c). Numerically, a=3/2, b=4/3, c=1/6 gives p=5/2 and p^2<q^2.
Sign of r in the general family: a-b=-(k^4-12k^2+4)/(2k(k^2+2)). The sign is irrelevant since only r^2 enters.
Signs of r' (e.g. r'=a-c should be c-a, and r'=-16, -14 in the example) are taken as absolute values. This is harmless.
'Eodem redeunt': item 2 is J. A. Euler's family with p=2k. I did not establish how item 1 maps onto that family; it is, however, an independently valid solution.

results.what: Parametric solutions α=8k^2/(2k^2-1)^2, β=2k^2 (or 1/(2k^2)) and α=1/(2k^2-1), β=8k^2/(2k^2-1)^2 making α(α+1)β(β+1)^2 a fourth power, plus the β→1/β symmetry
results.modern_name: rational points/parametrizations on a quartic surface; abc(a+b+c)=1

results.what: If kx(mx^2+n) is a square at x=a then at x=n/(ma)
results.modern_name: involution on the curve y^2=kx(mx^2+n) (translation by 2-torsion point / x→n/(mx))

results.what: (p^2-q^2)(q^2-r^2)=fourth power, with examples and linear maps multiplying the value by 16
results.modern_name: Diophantine problem; linear automorphisms of a quartic form

results.what: Reduction q=a+b, r=a-b, p=a+b+2c from abc(a+b+c)=1; polynomial family p=(k^2+2)^3, q=(k^2-2)(k^2+2)^2, r=(k^2-2)(k^4-12k^2+4)
results.modern_name: parametric family; equivalent to Heron triangles with square area
rational triangles whose area is a square (Heron's formula)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine Eulerian Diophantine manipulations, already printed in Opera postuma (1862, E806). All claims check except the '±' slip.

checkable.asserts: β→1/β multiplies by a fourth power (== 0)
all numerical examples are fourth powers
p formula in the general family (== 0 for k>sqrt2)

transcription_corrections: No substantive misreadings found. Note only that the 'r' in the general family and the r' values carry a suppressed minus sign; this is in Euler's text itself, not a transcription error.
In 'Hinc porro colligimus p'=2a+4b+2c, vel', the second line is p'=a+2b+c, q'=a+c, r'=a-c (halved), as transcribed.
